content: I haven't tried the env with solr nor upgraded yet, but I will and then let u know if it works.
Good news! At least on a new installation of Dataverse, I'm able to switch to Solr 9.11 and indexing still works. This might be the easiest thing rather than messing with JVM options.

This is the change I made:

[root@ip-172-31-37-44 dataverse-demo]# diff -u compose.yml.orig compose.yml
--- compose.yml.orig    2026-11-24 16:22:45.770073105 +0000
+++ compose.yml 2026-11-24 16:23:03.741314774 +0000
@@ -135,7 +135,7 @@
   solr:
     container_name: "solr"
     hostname: "solr"
-    image: solr:9.8.0
+    image: solr:9.11.0
     depends_on:
       - solr_initializer
     restart: on-failure
[root@ip-172-31-37-44 dataverse-demo]#

I confirmed I'm running 9.11.0 with this:

curl http://localhost:8983/solr/admin/info/system | jq '.lucene."solr-spec-version"'

I checked and Solr is running on a version of Java that isn't vulnerable:

$ sudo docker exec -it solr java --version
openjdk 17.0.21.1 2026-11-17
OpenJDK Runtime Environment Temurin-17.0.21.1+2 (build 17.0.21.1+2)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM Temurin-17.0.21.1+2 (build 17.0.21.1+2, mixed mode, sharing)

I just sent an advisory but I didn't link back to this topic because I get a bit nervous about talking about security vulnerabilities in a public channel like this.

  • #zulip > #security cleanup
  • #zulip > private channel for security?
